Q: QSslSocket: SSL support not available despite OpenSSL DLLs present (Qt 5.2.1, Windows, MinGW) A:

I spent a lot of time trying to fix the QSslSocket: SSL support not available error in my Qt 5.2.1 project on Windows. I tried different versions of OpenSSL DLLs (1.0.1, 1.0.2), placing them in the build folder, and messing with the PATH environment variable, but nothing worked.

As a beginner, I found it very difficult to debug why Qt couldn't "see" the libraries or why there were symbol conflicts.

My Solution:

Instead of fighting with the old Qt/OpenSSL integration, I decided to bypass QSslSocket entirely and use libcurl with mbedtls as the SSL backend.

It turned out to be much easier to manage because:

1. mbedtls is very lightweight compared to OpenSSL.

2. It's easier to link statically or find compatible binaries.

3. I stopped worrying about whether my Qt version was compiled with specific OpenSSL flags.

Here is how I set it up:

1. Getting the libraries

I used vcpkg to get the libraries because it handles all dependencies automatically. This was a lifesaver for me.

2. Simple Code Example

Here is a basic way to make an HTTPS GET request using libcurl instead of Qt's network classes.

Note: The downside is that you can't use QNetworkAccessManager signals/slots easily with this. You'll have to run curl in a separate QThread or use its multi-interface if you don't want to block the UI.

If you are stuck on an old Qt version like 5.2.1 and OpenSSL is giving you a headache, I highly recommend this "external" approach!

Q: How can I show lines in common (reverse diff)? A:

This is pretty easy using diff's built-in [old|new|unchanged]-line-format options:

diff --unchanged-line-format='%L' old.txt new.txt

These options are also useful for finding unique lines in one (or both) of the files. So to show lines in old.txt that aren't in new.txt:

diff --old-line-format='%L' old.txt new.txt

If want to compare the output of two commands or if you want to pre-filter files, you can use command substitution:

# Show common lines, excluding lines containing "badtext"
diff --unchanged-line-format='%L' <(grep -v "badtext" old.txt) <(grep -v "badtext" new.txt)

# Sort the files before showing the common lines:
diff --unchanged-line-format='%L' <(sort old.txt) <(sort new.txt)
